question: Which type of dog bed suits the way my dog sleeps?
answer_html: Watch how they lie down tonight; many dogs settle the same way every time. Curlers tuck their nose under their tail and press their back into something, so they want walls: try nest and donut beds. Leaners rest a chin on the sofa arm, so they want a bolster or a dog sofa bed. Sprawlers lie flat on their side and want open surface, like a dog mattress. Dogs who run hot may prefer a raised mesh bed, with air moving underneath. Still unsure? The Bed Finder starts with exactly this question.

question: What size dog bed do I need?
answer_html: With your dog lying on their side, measure from nose to the base of the tail and add 15 to 20cm. Then check what the bed's measurement means. On walled and bolstered beds it's usually the outside, and the sides take up part of it, so compare with the sleeping area where we list it, or measure your dog curled up. Between two sizes, size up. If a measurement is missing or unclear, send us their breed and weight and we'll tell you honestly which size fits. The size guide goes into more detail.

question: What's the difference between memory foam and fibre-filled beds?
answer_html: Foam spreads weight and keeps its shape; fibre feels soft and cosy, but loose filling can shift and pack down. Our orthopaedic beds are built on foam: memory foam, crumb memory foam, gel memory foam or profiled egg-crate foam, and some put memory foam over an egg-crate layer. Many nest and bolster beds are fibre-filled by design, for dogs who want to sink in rather than be held up. Neither is right for every dog. Product pages describe what's inside each bed, and if one isn't clear, ask us. What's inside our beds explains each filling in plain English.

question: Will an orthopaedic bed help my dog's arthritis or stiff joints?
answer_html: A bed is for comfort. It isn't a treatment and won't replace veterinary care, so please keep talking to your vet. What a bed can change is the effort involved. Foam spreads their weight across the surface instead of letting hips and elbows sink through towards the floor. A low or open front means stepping in rather than climbing over a wall. A non-slip base helps keep the bed from sliding on smooth floors. Our beds for older dogs and our guide to helping an older dog sleep well go further.

question: Can I put a dog bed in the washing machine?
answer_html: Usually the cover, never the foam. Most covers come off, and many machine wash at 30°C. Follow the sewn-in care label on each cover, and let every part air-dry fully before it goes back on. The foam itself should never be washed or soaked. Coated wipe-clean fabrics are different: wipe them for everyday marks and check the label before washing, because detergent and machine washing can affect some waterproof finishes. The open mesh beds, Windermere and Bassenthwaite, have no cover at all; you wipe or rinse them and let them dry. Our care and washing guide covers the rest.

question: Which beds cope with accidents, wet coats and muddy paws?
answer_html: Look for one of two things. Several foam beds, including Coniston, Borrowdale and Scafell, have a waterproof inner liner between the cover and the foam, so a wet coat or an accident stops at the liner instead of soaking into the core. Others are waterproof on the outside and wipe clean, such as the Wasdale mattress and the Crummock Waterproof Nest. The wipe-clean ones are together in waterproof dog beds.

question: Are your dog beds chew-proof?
answer_html: No, and we'd rather be straight with you: none of our beds is sold as chew-proof. The 100-night trial has damage exclusions, and the 5-year foam guarantee doesn't cover pet damage. If your dog pulls filling out, a raised mesh bed such as Bassenthwaite has no foam core or loose filling inside, though no bed is indestructible. Tell us about your dog before you order and we'll give you an honest view of what's likely to suit.

question: What if my dog won't sleep on it?
answer_html: On most of our beds, it comes back. They include a 100-night sleep trial from delivery: if it isn't right, contact us within the 100 nights and we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. Before you decide, give it time. Plenty of dogs take a while to swap a familiar bed for a new one, and a blanket that smells of home helps. The trial page has the step-by-step and some settling-in tips.

question: Are any products not covered by the 100-night trial?
answer_html: Three kinds of product, and each product page says so. Outdoor dog houses and day beds have a 30-day change-of-mind window, with return at your cost, instead of the trial. The personalised Rydal bed is made to order with your dog's name, so it's excluded from the trial and from change-of-mind returns. The Whinlatter car seat is a travel accessory: check the returns terms or ask us before ordering. Your statutory rights are unaffected, and if anything arrives faulty, damaged or not as described, your full legal rights apply.

question: Does free collection work if I'm not on the UK mainland?
answer_html: The trial's free collection is from UK mainland addresses. If you live elsewhere in the UK, such as Northern Ireland or one of the islands, please contact us before you order. We'll tell you how a return would work for your address, so you know where you stand before you spend anything.

question: What does the 5-year foam guarantee cover?
answer_html: It applies only to beds whose product page says so. They're all memory foam beds, such as Buttermere, Ambleside and Ennerdale, though not every memory foam product has it. On those beds the foam core has a 5-year no-flatten guarantee under normal domestic use, subject to the guarantee terms. Cover wear and pet damage are not included. It comes on top of the 100-night trial rather than replacing it. If a product page doesn't mention the guarantee, that product doesn't have it.

question: How much is delivery?
answer_html: Free standard UK delivery applies to orders over £40, and every bed in our current range is priced above £40, so a single bed qualifies on its own. The delivery options for your order, and any cost, are shown at checkout before you pay. Timings are covered on our delivery and returns page.

question: When will my bed arrive?
answer_html: Delivery timings, and any lead time for a particular product, are set out in our shipping policy, linked from our delivery and returns page. The options for your order are shown at checkout. Personalised beds are made to order with your dog's name, so order in good time, especially before Christmas, and check the spelling. If you need a bed by a particular date, ask us before you order.

question: Can I ask you before I order?
answer_html: Please do. We'd much rather you asked before you buy than after. Send your dog's breed and weight and we'll tell you honestly which size fits. For crate and boot beds, send the inside measurements of the crate base or boot floor. For outdoor dog houses and day beds, ask us for the exact dimensions before ordering. It all goes through our contact page.
